evidence.text:
Bubblesort is a popular, but inefﬁcient, sorting algorithm. It works by repeatedly
swapping adjacent elements that are out of order.

Bubble sort repeatedly examines adjacent records and exchanges an out-of-order pair. For
ascending order, swap only when the left key is greater than the right key. Each exchange
removes exactly one inversion because the two records are adjacent and only their relative order
changes. A nonadjacent exchange does not have that same one-inversion property.

Problem 2-2 scans from right to left in each inner loop. The smallest key in the remaining suffix
moves left through neighboring positions. After the pass for outer index i, A[i] contains a
smallest remaining key, and the finalized prefix grows by one.
Many presentations scan left to right instead. That version moves a largest remaining key
toward the right end and grows a finalized suffix. Both are bubble sort, but their intermediate
arrays and invariants differ. A trace question must specify the scan direction and what counts as
one pass.
